stances.claim: Comelec committed grave abuse of discretion in disqualifying Smartmatic TIM without due process and in violation of the GPRA and Comelec's IRR -- an act void and deemed nonexistent.

Under the doctrine of operative fact, even a void act can produce consequences in good faith that cannot be erased; here, the strict 2025-election timeline is a 'higher public good,' so the decision applies prospectively without invalidating the bidding already done.
stances.rhetorical_move: doctrine-application reasoning to balance rights and public good

stances.claim: The doctrine does not render Smartmatic's petition a 'Pyrrhic victory': it may still participate in future biddings (e.g., 2028) unless properly disqualified after observance of its rights, the GPRA, and the IRR.
A Comelec motion for reconsideration would be 'a waste of time and resources' given the unanimous Court -- and CJ supports the rule of law and due process regardless of any view on Smartmatic.

Rene A.V. Saguisag's 'mortal life may have ended, but his immortal work shall forever be etched in the pantheon of heroes' -- profound, tenacious, honest, humble, and one who 'opted to be poor, to serve the poor, and to remain poor until his death.'

Though viewed by many as a 'leftist,' RAVS was 'not a political creature' -- shown by his reluctance to run for the Senate, and his refusal to seek reelection despite favorable surveys; his passion was 'to fight for what is right and against what is wrong, regardless of who and what is on the other side.'

one_paragraph_summary: The Supreme Court, in a unanimous decision penned by Justice Jose Midas P. Marquez, struck down the Comelec en banc's Nov. 29, 2023 resolution disqualifying Smartmatic TIM Corp. from any public bidding (especially for the 2025 automated election system), holding that the agency committed grave abuse of discretion by disqualifying Smartmatic without due process and in violation of the Government Procurement Reform Act (RA 9184) and Comelec's own IRR -- Comelec had acted on information from the US Department of Justice about an ongoing investigation of alleged irregularities in the 2016 AES procurement under former Comelec chair Andres D. Bautista. Yet the Court did not invalidate the bidding already won by the joint venture led by Miru Systems for 2025. The reason is the doctrine of operative fact: acts done in good faith before a determination of unconstitutionality produce consequences that cannot always be erased -- the void act is set aside but its effects sustained where a higher public good (here, the strict 2025-election timeline) so requires. Smartmatic's victory is not Pyrrhic -- it may participate in future biddings (such as the 2028 presidential elections) unless properly disqualified after due process, the GPRA, and the Comelec IRR are faithfully observed. CJ thinks any Comelec motion for reconsideration would be 'a waste of time and resources' and, while taking no position on Smartmatic substantively, anchors his view in the rule of law: 'I may not agree with what you say, but I will defend to the death your right to say it.' The column then pivots to a tribute to the late Rene A.V. Saguisag -- 'profound, tenacious, honest, and humble' -- who 'opted to be poor, to serve the poor, and to remain poor until his death.' CJ recalls offering in 1961 to help RAVS get elected NUS president; RAVS declined and asked CJ to nominate Raul S. Roco. After RAVS's Ledesma Law Office stint, CJ invited him to be a partner; RAVS preferred solo practice and later collaborated with CJ and Dean Antonio H. Abad Jr. on pro bono cases. Viewed as a 'leftist' by many, RAVS was no political creature -- initially reluctant to run for the Senate and firmly refusing reelection despite favorable surveys. CJ last saw him alive on April 9, when he was acclaimed as one of 13 'Haligi' of the Bantayog ng mga Bayani Foundation at the UP-University Hotel; though wheelchair-bound and 'numbed by illness,' RAVS 'manfully raised his clenched fist' for each honoree and stretched his weakened right arm for 'Bayan Ko.' 'Compadre Rene (the baptism ninong of my daughter Celine), rest in Heaven with my Leni in the peace and love of the Lord.'
